fib: ______ is a separation procedure in which macromolecules like polypeptides are separated from smaller molecules of solvent, salts, minerals and other metabolites.
Dialysis

______ are known by examining the amino acid composition of all the fragments generated.
Fragments having cysteine residues
Fragments having cysteine residues are known by examining the amino acid composition of all the fragments generated.
______ are the ones used in enzyme classification.
systematic names
The systematic names are the ones used in enzyme classification.
______ is a widely used analytical separation procedure for proteins and peptides (among many other charged biomolecules).
Electrophoretic technique
Electrophoretic technique is a widely used analytical separation procedure for proteins and peptides (among many other charged biomolecules).
______ is called a dimer while one with few subunits is often called an oligomer.
Protein with two subunits
Protein with two subunits is called a dimer while one with few subunits is often called an oligomer.
______ refers to the overall three-dimensional arrangement of all atoms in a protein.
tertiary structure
The tertiary structure refers to the overall three-dimensional arrangement of all atoms in a protein.
______ are the building blocks of proteins.
Amino acids
Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins.
______ are the cellular organelles that are known for protein synthesis.
Ribosomes
Ribosomes are the cellular organelles that are known for protein synthesis.
______ is the force that causes nonpolar substances and nonpolar portions of amphipathic molecules (molecules with both polar and nonpolar regions e.g. proteins) to minimise their contact with water.
Hydrophobic interaction

Hydrophobic interaction is the force that causes nonpolar substances and nonpolar portions of amphipathic molecules (molecules with both polar and nonpolar regions e.g. proteins) to minimise their contact with water.
______ refers to the arrangement of polypeptide chains in multichain protein.
Quaternary structure of protein
Quaternary structure of protein refers to the arrangement of polypeptide chains in multichain protein.
______ are the class of proteins that accelerate the rate of biological reactions.
Catalytic proteins
Catalytic proteins are the class of proteins that accelerate the rate of biological reactions.
______ is the functional, folded conformations of proteins.
native conformation
The native conformation is the functional, folded conformations of proteins.
